transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've been feeling really down and depressed lately. It's been going on constantly for about 10 months now, and I just can't seem to shake this heavy sadness.
Have you experienced these feelings of sadness every single day for the past 10 months, or have there been periods of a few weeks or more where you felt like your normal self?

No, there haven't been any breaks at all. I've felt this heavy sadness every single day for the entire ten months, without a single day of feeling like my old self. It just never seems to lift, not even for a moment.

latest_inference.note: Previously, both Major Depressive Disorder and Persistent Depressive Disorder were considered. Given that the patient reports a continuous, unremitting period of low mood for 10 months without any symptom-free intervals, Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia) becomes the primary diagnostic consideration, as it is characterized by a chronic depressed mood lasting for at least two years in adults (or one year in children/adolescents), whereas the current duration of 10 months is approaching the threshold for the diagnosis if the symptoms persist.
